item.title: A high spatiotemporal resolution atmospheric motion vector dataset from Fengyun-4B Geostationary High-speed Imager observations for 15 tropical cyclones over the western North Pacific and South China Sea (2022–2025)
item.description:
A high spatiotemporal resolution atmospheric motion vector dataset from Fengyun-4B Geostationary High-speed Imager observations for 15 tropical cyclones over the western North Pacific and South China Sea (2022–2025)
Pan Xia, Min Min, Jun Li, Na Xu, Di Di, Yan-An Liu, Gang Wang, Zijing Liu, and Yongqiang Chen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-606,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
This study presents a validated FY-4B minute-scale mesoscale AMV dataset for 15 tropical cyclones (2022–2025), offering 3-km VIS and 24-km IRX vectors at 1/2/6/7 min intervals. It provides unprecedented observations of inner-core, rainband, and outflow structures. Evaluated against radiosondes and ERA5, VIS biases are 2.34 and 1.62 m/s, and IRX biases are 2.21 and 0.31 m/s, respectively. The dataset supports detailed monitoring of TC structural evolution and short-term intensity change.

item.title: MioMG: Reconstructing robust ocean temperatures from Miocene foraminiferal Mg/Ca records
item.description:
MioMG: Reconstructing robust ocean temperatures from Miocene foraminiferal Mg/Ca records
Sindia M. Sosdian, Karlos G. D. Kochhann, Anya V. Hess, Clara Bolton, Anna Joy Drury, Emily J. Judd, Wolfgang Kuhnt, Caroline H. Lear, Paul Minton, Alexandra Auderset, Sevasti Modestou, and Ann Holbourn
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-697,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
From 23.0 and 5.3 Million years ago (Miocene epoch), atmospheric carbon dioxide levels were similar to those projected for the future. To assess their impact on global climate, it is crucial to robustly reconst ocean temperatures using proxies, such as the magnesium-to-calcium (Mg/Ca) ratio in microfossils called foraminifera. Here we reevaluate global Miocene foraminiferal Mg/Ca records, and use revised calibrations to recalculate, assessing uncertainties, upper and deep ocean temperatures.

item.title: A long-term multiscale Critical Zone dataset integrating environmental monitoring and an open-air laboratory: The Alento River Catchment Observatory
item.description:
A long-term multiscale Critical Zone dataset integrating environmental monitoring and an open-air laboratory: The Alento River Catchment Observatory
Nunzio Romano, Harry Vereecken, Heye R. Bogena, Giorgio Cassiani, Matteo Censini, Giovanna Armiento, Marco Proposito, Lorenzo De Silvestri, Eyal Ben Dor, Nicolas Francos, Christian Massari, János Mészáros, Tünde Takáts, Caterina Mazzitelli, Benedetto Sica, Ugo Lazzaro, and Paolo Nasta
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-725,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Understanding how climate and land-use change affect water resources requires observations that connect processes from soils and vegetation to groundwater and streams. The Alento dataset is presented that integrates environmental monitoring with targeted field observations across multiple Critical Zone components and scales. The dataset offers a distinctive resource for studying water storage and movement, evaluating environmental models, and improving understanding of water-limited regions.
